title: Single-site object cohomology equivalence normalized on Ext cocycles
statement: Let C be a category, J a Grothendieck topology on C admitting abelian sheafification, and suppose Ext exists for abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let F be an abelian sheaf, I an injective resolution of F [def-sp-injective-resolutions], q a nonnegative integer, and V an object of C. Put P(V) equal to the sheafification of the free abelian presheaf on yoneda(V), and put K equal to the complex of sections of I over V. There exists an additive equivalence e from Ext^q(P(V),F) to H^q(K) such that for every a:P(V)→I^q satisfying a≫d=0, e(I.extMk(a)) is the homology projection of the cycle whose underlying section is a evaluated at the sheafified identity generator. The cycle and its class are explicitly constructed as sheafCocycleSection and sheafCocycleSectionClass; they are not arbitrary existential choices.

proof.text: Compose the sheafification adjunction, the free abelian adjunction on presheaves, and Yoneda to identify Hom(P(V),A) additively with A(V). Its value is evaluation at the sheafified identity generator, by unfolding the adjunction units. Postcomposition naturality intertwines all differentials. Lift sections to the sheaf morphism universe and obtain a degreewise isomorphism of the nonnegative Hom complex with the lifted section complex. The cycles inclusion is monic, so naturality of the homology projection proves the formula on explicit cycle classes. The same argument with the universe-lift homology comparison identifies a lifted cycle class with the lift of the original class.

Use the injective-resolution Ext cocycle API [lem-weil-pbc-ext-via-injective-resolution] directly. The additive map from closed maps X to I^q to Ext^q(X,F), defined by extMk, is surjective by extMk_surjective. In positive degrees its kernel is exactly the incoming boundaries by extMk_eq_zero_iff. In degree zero, extEquivCohomologyClass and fromSingleMk_mem_coboundaries_iff identify zero classes with maps factoring through I.cochainComplex.X(-1), which is zero; thus the kernel is zero, equal to the image of the zero incoming differential. The quotient-group liftEquiv and the short-complex abHomologyIso give an additive equivalence normalized on extMk. Specialize X to P(V), compose with the termwise evaluation homology isomorphism, the universe-lift homology comparison, and ULift.down. The cycle projection compatibility proved in the first step gives the exact sheafCocycleSectionClass formula.

from.place: Construct cocycle-normalized equivalences from the termwise adjunction and injective-resolution Ext computation (proof steps 1 and 2).

lean.statement:
theorem objectCohomology_resolution_cocycle_equivalence
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{v}]
    [HasExt.{w} (Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{v})]
    (F : Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{v}) (I : InjectiveResolution F) (q : ℕ) (V : C) :
    ∃ (e : Sheaf.H' F q V ≃+ (sheafSectionComplex J I.cocomplex V).homology q),
      ∀ (a : (presheafToSheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{v}).obj
        (yoneda.obj V ⋙ AddCommGrpCat.free) ⟶ I.cocomplex.X q)
        (ha : a ≫ I.cocomplex.d q (q + 1) = 0),
        e (I.extMk a (q + 1) rfl ha) =
          sheafCocycleSectionClass J I.cocomplex q V a ha
